Scenario.Name: Largo
Scenario.Author: EcoKnow
Scenario.Description: Hand-authored 80x40 catchment-style water test scenario based on the Largo geographical map: two 2-tile-wide freshwater rivers descend from the north, merge into a single river that first sweeps east and then runs south to a 2-tile-wide sand band wrapping the bay in a crescent. A separate 1-tile-wide tributary descends through the right-side crops region: it enters at (col 67, row 9), L-elbow staircases southwest down to (col 62, row 16), then runs straight south at col 62 through to the bay, passing through 2 estuary cells over the sand band and discharging via 2 river-mouth cells into the seawater. The 1-tile-wide channel uses L-elbow placement at every direction change so the dual-grid autotiler never selects a diagonal-only tile (no pair of freshwater-bearing cells is diagonally adjacent without an orthogonal connector). The grass area between the central voids and the new tributary (rows 22-27, cols 49-61) and the small grass patches near the new tributary (rows 20-21, cols 57-61) have been converted to crops to give the new tributary visual breathing room. The left golf field (cols 0-20, rows 17-21) and the right golf field (cols 75-78, rows 15-21) remain. Below the sand band sits the seawater bay (also crescent-shaped). Two 3x3 Overflow patches (zone 8) sit in the bay: the first at cols 48-50 / rows 31-33 — directly below the void/crops land boundary at col 47-48, with one buffer seawater cell (51, 33) separating it from the right-side sand at (52, 33); the second at cols 31-33 / rows 31-33 — sharing the first patch's top row, three cells west of the main river-mouth at col 36 and four rows south of the upper sand band at row 27 (chebyshev-4 from the nearest sand, giving a wider buffer that suits the parallel sand edge). Overflow is a logical marker, not a renderable terrain: cells render as ordinary seawater, and the brown tint is produced by ElevationMap baking a separate overflow distance field that EK_Water samples on the sea branch. Freshwater renders over Soil; seawater renders over Sand (per TerrainPriority.ZoneTerrainStacks). The Freshwater terrain reuses a duplicate of the seawater tileset until a dedicated freshwater tileset exists. SOURCE OF TRUTH: Map_Largo.csv (zone definitions + tile layout) and the largo_*.csv matrix files (one per zone). This JSON is a snapshot of those sources; regenerate it if the source CSVs change.

WinConditions.Title: Inspect Water Features
WinConditions.Description: Visual test scenario: confirm the two freshwater rivers merge cleanly, the merged river bends right then runs south to the sand, and the crescent-shaped sand band & bay tile correctly at every boundary.
